Key Takeaways

AT&T shares closed [25%] below their March high on Oct. 21, and Bank of America still sees them reaching $34, [55%] above that close.

The stock fell after a third-quarter report with 20% adjusted EPS growth and a raised 2026 outlook, with SpaceX's Starlink push into mobile hanging over the carriers.

Analysts expect normalized EPS to climb from $2.12 in 2025 to $2.92 in 2028, and the stock trades a little below its 5-year average forward P/E.

BofA's target works out to about 14x forward earnings, close to the stock's 5-year high, so the call is plausible but stretched.

AT&T (T:NYSE) just posted its best service revenue growth in more than four years and raised its 2026 earnings outlook. The stock sank anyway, closing at $21.91 yesterday, 25% below its March 27 closing high of $29.10.

On Oct. 22, Bank of America analyst Michael Funk reiterated his Buy rating and $34 price target, 55% above that close.

Strong quarter, sour reaction

SpaceX (SPCX:NASDAQ) hung over the report, as investors weigh what a Starlink push into mobile could mean for carriers.

Revenue rose 5.3% to $32.3 billion, adjusted EPS climbed to $0.65 from $0.54, and management now expects about $2.40 for 2026, up from $2.25 to $2.35.

But investors zeroed in on slower postpaid phone growth and a 4% drop in fiber ARPU.

BofA is sticking with $34

Funk's case rests on convergence, AT&T's push to sell customers wireless and fiber together. Ahead of the report, he noted that "AT&T remains disciplined in wireless despite ongoing competitive intensity around the iPhone launch."

title: Is AT&T Worth Buying as Fiber Growth Offsets Rising Leverage Risks?
detail:
Is AT&T Worth Buying as Fiber Growth Offsets Rising Leverage Risks?
Aritra Chatterjee
Thu, October 22, 2026 at 6:52 AM MST 3 min read
T
ECHO
VZ
TMUS
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

AT&T Inc. T is pairing faster fiber and wireless growth with a balance sheet that became more leveraged after its EchoStar spectrum purchase. Third-quarter 2026 results showed that the core connectivity strategy is gaining traction, but the investment case is not one-sided.

The question for investors is whether improving service revenues, a modest valuation and shareholder returns provide enough compensation for legacy declines, higher interest costs and a longer deleveraging path.

AT&T's Fiber Expansion Strengthens the Growth Case

AT&T added more than 1 million Advanced Connectivity customers in the third quarter, including 769,000 Internet net additions across consumer and business accounts. Fiber additions totaled 442,000, while fixed wireless added 327,000 customers.

Advanced home Internet service revenue increased 23.4% year over year. The convergence rate reached 42.8%, and AT&T added about 350,000 converged relationships during the quarter. The company reached 39.7 million fiber locations and remains on track to exceed 40 million by year-end 2026.

T's Wireless Gains Support Recurring Service Revenue

Wireless service revenues rose 5% year over year, driven by subscriber growth and pricing. AT&T added 379,000 postpaid phone subscribers, while postpaid phone average revenue per user increased about 4%. Management continues to expect Advanced Connectivity service revenue growth of at least 5% in 2026.

T-Mobile US, Inc. TMUS is also expanding its broadband footprint through fiber partnerships alongside its 5G broadband business. Verizon Communications Inc. VZ, with a large wireless base and fiber broadband operations, remains another relevant benchmark for investors comparing converged connectivity strategies.

AT&T's Valuation Looks Modest Against Key Benchmarks

AT&T trades at 2.1X trailing 12-month enterprise value to sales, below its five-year median of 2.26X. The multiple also sits well below the Zacks sub-industry's 8.15X and the broader sector's 8.31X.

The shares trade at 9.4X forward earnings, while the PEG ratio is 0.97. Those measures support the value case, but a low multiple alone does not eliminate execution risk when leverage is elevated and legacy operations are shrinking.

T's Debt and Legacy Declines Keep Risks Elevated

Legacy revenues fell 24.5% year over year in the third quarter, while Legacy EBITDA declined 26.7%. Copper retirement should reduce costs over time, but the transition continues to weigh on reported revenues and earnings before the remaining expense base is fully removed.

Net debt rose to $149.8 billion, and net debt to adjusted EBITDA increased to 3.13X from 2.68X in the second quarter after the $23 billion EchoStar spectrum purchase. AT&T still targets leverage near 2.5X during 2029. Capital investment, dividends and buybacks will continue competing for cash while higher interest payments pressure financial flexibility.

title: AT&T Stock Falls 13.4% in a Month. Is the Drop a Buying Opportunity?

AT&T Stock Falls 13.4% in a Month. Is the Drop a Buying Opportunity?

AT&T Inc. T shares have fallen 13.4% in the past four weeks even as third-quarter 2026 operating trends improved. The pullback raises the question of whether valuation now better compensates investors for the company's execution risks.

Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Fiber expansion, wireless subscriber gains and a higher earnings outlook support the case for stabilization. Elevated leverage, promotional spending and continued legacy declines keep the setup from becoming a straightforward buying call.

AT&T's One-Month Slide Tests the Bull Case

AT&T reported third-quarter adjusted earnings of 65 cents per share, up 20.4% year over year, while revenues increased 5.3% to $32.32 billion. Both measures topped the Zacks Consensus Estimate.

AT&T Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise
AT&T Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

AT&T Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | AT&T Inc. Quote

Management also raised its 2026 adjusted earnings outlook to around $2.40 per share from $2.25-$2.35. The stronger operating picture contrasts with the recent share weakness, though the decline should not be tied to any single factor.

T's Fiber Momentum Still Supports Service Growth

AT&T added 769,000 Internet connections across consumer and business accounts, including 442,000 fiber additions and 327,000 fixed wireless additions. Advanced home Internet service revenues increased 23.4% year over year.

Fiber reach rose to 39.7 million locations. AT&T remains on track to exceed 40 million locations by year-end 2026, giving the company a broader base for convergence with wireless services.

AT&T's Wireless Gains Face Promotion Pressure

Wireless service revenues rose 5% year over year and AT&T added 379,000 postpaid phone subscribers. Postpaid phone churn reached 0.92%, up from 0.86% in the second quarter.

Promotional discounts and introductory fiber pricing remain a trade-off. Fiber average revenue per user declined 4% year over year. T-Mobile US TMUS is expanding its broadband portfolio through fiber partnerships, adding another competitive route into home Internet. Verizon Communications Inc. VZ continues to pursue mobility and broadband convergence, making its network expansion another relevant benchmark for AT&T.

T's Debt Load Limits Near-Term Financial Flexibility

Net debt climbed to $149.8 billion after the $23 billion EchoStar spectrum purchase. Net debt to adjusted EBITDA increased to 3.13X from 2.68X in the second quarter.

AT&T still targets leverage in the 2.5X range during 2029. Capital investment, dividends, repurchases and customer acquisition spending all compete for cash, making debt reduction an important part of the recovery case.

title: AT&T's Q3 Earnings Call Refines Fiber Spending and Pricing Strategy
detail:
AT&T's Q3 Earnings Call Refines Fiber Spending and Pricing Strategy
Zacks Equity Research
Thu, October 22, 2026 at 6:00 AM MST 4 min read
T
Trade AT&T on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

AT&T Inc. T outlined lower capital investment while maintaining its fiber expansion target on its third-quarter 2026 earnings call. Executives defended introductory broadband pricing to build converged relationships.

Adjusted earnings of $0.65 beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $0.61, while revenues of $32.32 billion exceeded the $31.68 billion estimate. Analysts focused on fiber penetration, cash generation and competition.

AT&T Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise
AT&T Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

AT&T Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | AT&T Inc. Quote

T Trims Long-Term Capital Investment

Chief financial officer Pascal Desroches projected $22-$23 billion in annual capital investment during 2027 and 2028, about $1 billion below the prior plan.

Desroches credited construction efficiencies and $300-$400 million in eliminated Mexico wireless investment, while retaining the target of more than 60 million fiber locations by 2030.

AT&T raised its 2026 adjusted earnings outlook to about $2.4 per share from $2.25-$2.35, primarily reflecting lower depreciation related to Mexico's held-for-sale treatment. Free cash flow targets remain $18 billion-plus for 2026, $19 billion-plus for 2027 and $21 billion-plus for 2028.

Desroches also warned of about $100 million in unfavorable vendor settlements and higher marketing costs during the fourth quarter.

AT&T Defends Fiber Pricing and Penetration

Chief executive officer John Stankey prioritized converged accounts over maximizing fiber revenue per customer. AT&T added approximately 350,000 such relationships, and 42.8% of advanced home internet customers also held postpaid wireless accounts.

Advanced Connectivity delivered 769,000 Internet net additions, including 442,000 fiber connections.

Desroches said that fiber average revenue per user fell 4% year over year due to introductory offers, convergence discounts and acquired Lumen customers. He expects a similar fourth-quarter decline.

When asked by a UBS analyst about fiber penetration, Stankey mentioned that project economics assume 40% terminal penetration, but management intends to exceed that level. He considers 50% achievable over time, supported by greater convergence.

T Faces Cash Conversion and Leverage Questions

A New Street Research analyst questioned working capital needs. Desroches explained that AT&T pays for customer devices upfront but recovers those costs over customer relationships, creating a cash drag as additions accelerate.

Answering Morgan Stanley, Desroches said that excluding Mexico would reduce annual cash flow by $400 million to $500 million. Higher interest costs also absorb some benefits from reduced investment.

title: Verizon Slides as SpaceX’s $8 Billion Spectrum Deal Clouds Wireless Pricing
detail:
Verizon Slides as SpaceX’s $8 Billion Spectrum Deal Clouds Wireless Pricing
Rexielyn Diaz
Thu, October 22, 2026 at 4:46 AM MST 4 min read

SPCX

Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Verizon Slides as SpaceX's $8 Billion Spectrum Deal Clouds Wireless Pricing ©Bilal Ahmed from Pexels and Iulian Catalin's Images via Canva
Key Takeaways

Verizon fell 2.2% to $44 on October 21 after AT&T slid on weaker fiber revenue per user.

Management expects mobility and broadband service revenue growth to approach 3% in Q3 and reach about 4% in Q4.

SpaceX's roughly $8 billion spectrum deal adds long-term competitive risk, though an 8.6x forward P/E already prices in plenty of skepticism.

The October 26 Q3 report will show whether service revenue acceleration and postpaid phone gains are holding up.

Telecom stocks rarely trade on a rival's fiber metrics. This week, Verizon (VZ:NYSE) did.

Shares fell 2.2% to $44 on October 21 after AT&T (T:NYSE) slid on weaker fiber revenue per user. Investors read that as a warning for the sector ahead of Verizon's own report on October 26.

The timing is awkward. Verizon has spent 2026 building one of the better turnaround stories in telecom, and the stock still shows a 14.7% total return this year.

Then SpaceX (SPCX:NASDAQ) bought its way into wireless spectrum, and the debate shifted from execution to competition.

The turnaround numbers so far

Q2 delivered the strongest evidence yet that the strategy is working:

Mobility and broadband service revenue grew 2.8%, even as total revenue dipped 0.7% to $34.3 billion.

Total postpaid phone net additions reached 184,000, and broadband added 348,000 customers.

Adjusted EPS rose 6.6% to $1.30, while free cash flow jumped 24% to $6.4 billion.

Management raised full-year guidance for the second straight quarter. CEO Dan Schulman described the results as evidence of a "structural inflection point" across the business.

Cash generation is what pays the dividend.

Verizon Communications (VZ): free cash flow, $ billions, fiscal 2021–2025 (TIKR)

That cash funds a $0.71 quarterly dividend plus $3.5 billion of buybacks through the first half.

SpaceX changes the long-term math

In early October, SpaceX agreed to buy up to 14 MHz of paired 800 MHz spectrum from Grain Management, reportedly valued near $8 billion, to support Starlink Mobile. Verizon, AT&T and T-Mobile US (TMUS:NASDAQ) all fell on the news.

Verizon already holds low-band spectrum in the 700 MHz and 850 MHz bands, so the asset gap is narrower than the headlines suggested. The SpaceX deal also still needs FCC approval.

The bigger question is pricing. A satellite rival does not need to match Verizon's network to pressure retention at the low end of the market.

Have investors treated the three carriers differently this year?

Verizon Communications (VZ): total return (%) vs AT&T and T-Mobile US, last 1 year (TIKR)

The SpaceX headline hit all three. Still, Verizon's improving subscriber trends give it more cushion than AT&T heading into earnings.

The Morning Bull - US Market Morning Update Thursday, Oct, 22 2026

US stocks look set to open weaker, with futures pointing lower as investors react to a sharp upside surprise in UK inflation. The move is feeding a more cautious mood around global central bank policy.

UK CPI printed at 3.5% in September, with core inflation at 2.8%, both above recent trends and prior readings. These numbers have raised expectations that tight policy in major economies may persist longer than markets had been assuming.

Higher for longer policy thinking tends to pressure longer term bond yields, which directly affects borrowing costs for US households and companies. That can compress valuation multiples for growth heavy indices and complicate earnings plans for capital intensive businesses.

The key question now is whether upcoming US data breaks or confirms this stickier inflation story, particularly initial jobless claims today and PMIs on Friday. If US numbers echo the UK pattern, investors may need to reassess how much policy relief is realistically priced in.

A dividend check is only as reliable as the cash behind it. The screen used here is simple: compare what a company actually brings in (free cash flow for ordinary businesses, funds from operations for REITs) with what it pays out, then check whether debt is filling the gap. That matters most to retired people who spend the income. Hospital landlord Medical Properties Trust (NYSE: MPT) now yields about 13.7% after its shares fell 44.05% this year. A yield that high often means the market is pricing in risk, and the stock may not be a bargain.

MY STOCKERS / Shutterstock.com

The quick test: a dividend starts to look unsustainable when the right cash measure only covers it, when free cash flow is shrinking, or when rising debt is quietly paying for the dividend alongside buybacks and deals (we laid out the full set of signals that a high yield is about to be cut in a free report on dividend traps).

Medical Properties Trust: A 13% Yield Built on a Collapsing Share Price

Medical Properties Trust owns hospitals and rents them to operators in the U.S., the U.K. and Europe. It now trades under the ticker MPT. It pays $0.09 per quarter, or $0.36 per year, while the stock trades at $2.63.
